references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where Joseph of Arimathea goes to Pilate and asks for Jesus' body: [ref:Matt 27:58|Matthew 27:58].
The parallel passage in Mark where Joseph of Arimathea ventures to Pilate and asks for Jesus' body: [ref:Mark 15:43|Mark 15:43].
In the Gospel of John, it is Joseph of Arimathea who asks Pilate to take down Jesus' body from the cross: [ref:Joh 19:38|John 19:38].
The context describing who Joseph of Arimathea was—a good and righteous man, a member of the Council, who had not consented to their decision and action: [ref:Luk 23:50-51|Luke 23:50-51].
The prophecy that the Lord's suffering servant would be buried with a rich man, which is fulfilled as the wealthy Joseph of Arimathea takes care of Jesus' body: [ref:Jes 53:9|Isaiah 53:9].
